idiom_name: Vapor route per page (app.get("orders") { req in ... })
implementation_notes: Vapor registers one closure per method and path - app.get("orders") { req in ... } - and the closure is the page controller: it reads req.parameters or req.content, calls the service and returns anything ResponseEncodable, typically a Leaf view through req.view.render or a Codable Content type. Path components can be constants, parameters (:name) or catch-alls, so the URL structure is declared at the route; shared behaviour goes into middleware (app.middleware.use) or grouped routes instead of a controller superclass. Vapor's RouteCollection controllers are optional packaging for many pages, not a requirement.
pitfalls: Handlers run on NIO event loops: blocking calls (synchronous DB drivers, large file I/O) must be moved off the loop or they stall every other request.
req.parameters.get returns an optional: force-unwrapping a route parameter traps on a malformed URL instead of producing a 400.
Request bodies are collected into memory up to a default limit (16 KB) unless the route opts into streaming, so a large form post returns 413 before the handler body runs.
